key_insight: Low-dimensional perovskite capping increases surface roughness while preserving electronic uniformity and suppressing aging-induced optoelectronic disorder.
engineering_relevance: Surface smoothness alone may be a poor quality metric when designing durable perovskite photovoltaics with electronically protective capping layers.
method: Form mixed-dimensional heterostructures using 5-tert-butyl-phenanthridinium-derived Ruddlesden–Popper capping layers.
Combine statistical AFM with spatially resolved confocal photoluminescence spectroscopy.
Compare morphology, emission, and quasi-Fermi level splitting before and after accelerated aging.
evidence_signal: Despite greater roughness and height asymmetry, capped films showed enhanced photoluminescence, reduced non-radiative recombination, and more spatially uniform radiative quasi-Fermi level splitting, largely retaining optoelectronic homogeneity during aging.
watch_item: The abstract does not report device efficiency, quantitative effect sizes, or aging conditions, limiting assessment of practical photovoltaic durability.
paper_title: Electronic-morphological decoupling in mixed-dimensional halide perovskite heterostructures
